text: If `config.Output` is nil, the log line is written to the Echo instance's logger output: `c.Logger().Output()` (middleware/logger.go, end of the returned handler). `c.Logger()` returns the per-request logger if set via `c.SetLogger(...)`, otherwise `e.Logger` — which `echo.New()` initializes to `log.New("echo")` (gommon log), whose output defaults to `os.Stdout`. That matches the field's doc comment "Optional. Default value os.Stdout." Note the nil check happens at write time, so `config.colorer.SetOutput(config.Output)` is set up with nil, but the actual write goes to the Echo logger's writer.

Fixed in middleware/proxy.go. Root cause: with an empty target list, `randomBalancer.Next` called `rand.Intn(0)` ("invalid argument to Intn" panic) and `roundRobinBalancer.Next` indexed `targets[0]` (index out of range). Both `Next` implementations now return nil when there are no targets, and `ProxyWithConfig` returns `echo.ErrServiceUnavailable` (503) when the balancer yields no target instead of dereferencing nil. Verified: `NewRandomBalancer(nil).Next`/`NewRoundRobinBalancer(nil).Next` return nil, the middleware responds 503 without panicking (also after removing all targets at runtime), and the full test suite passes, including `go test -race ./middleware/`.

It returns `echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusInternalServerError, i.(error).Error())` — i.e. a 500 "Internal Server Error" HTTPError whose message is the string form of the pooled value, obtained by asserting the value to `error` (middleware/decompress.go, in the `case GZIPEncoding:` branch of `DecompressWithConfig`). The pool's `New` function only ever returns a `*gzip.Reader` or an `error`, so the non-`*gzip.Reader` case is the error case; note that if the pooled value were neither, the `i.(error)` assertion itself would panic rather than return the HTTPError.

`MethodOverride()` returns an `echo.MiddlewareFunc` — specifically `MethodOverrideWithConfig(DefaultMethodOverrideConfig)`. That middleware only overrides the method for `POST` requests (per its doc comment: "For security reasons, only `POST` method can be overridden"), replacing `req.Method` with the non-empty value from the configured getter (default: the `X-HTTP-Method-Override` header), then calls `next(c)`.
#1 is fixed and verified (middleware/proxy.go: balancers return nil with no targets, middleware returns 503 instead of panicking; full suite + -race pass).
#4 (router.go / TestRouterNoRoutablePath) is still being diagnosed; ETA ~12 minutes.

In `redirect(config RedirectConfig, cb redirectLogic)` (middleware/redirect.go), when `config.Skipper` is nil it sets `config.Skipper = DefaultTrailingSlashConfig.Skipper` — note: the *trailing-slash* middleware's default skipper, not `DefaultRedirectConfig.Skipper`. Behaviorally it makes no difference here, since `DefaultTrailingSlashConfig.Skipper` and `DefaultRedirectConfig.Skipper` are both `DefaultSkipper` (which always returns false).

`limitedReader.Read` (middleware/body_limit.go) returns the `n` from the underlying reader along with `echo.ErrStatusRequestEntityTooLarge` — i.e. `(n, echo.ErrStatusRequestEntityTooLarge)` — as soon as the cumulative `r.read` exceeds `r.limit`. The error is the pre-allocated 413 HTTPError (`ErrStatusRequestEntityTooLarge`), not a plain error.
`DefaultBodyDumpConfig.Skipper` is `DefaultSkipper` (middleware/body_dump.go) — the shared skipper that always returns false, so nothing is skipped by default.
The `bytes_in` tag writes `"0"`: it reads the `Content-Length` header and, if that header is empty, substitutes the string `"0"` before writing it (middleware/logger.go, `case "bytes_in":`).

`MethodFromQuery(param string)` returns a `MethodOverrideGetter` — a `func(c echo.Context) string` closure that returns `c.QueryParam(param)`, i.e. the value of the named query-string parameter (middleware/method_override.go).

In `DecompressWithConfig` (middleware/decompress.go), when `config.Skipper` is nil it sets `config.Skipper = DefaultGzipConfig.Skipper` — the *Gzip* middleware's default skipper (again a copy/paste of the same `DefaultSkipper` that always returns false, so behavior is unaffected).

It panics: `BodyLimitWithConfig` calls `bytes.Parse(config.Limit)` and, if that returns an error, does `panic(fmt.Errorf("echo: invalid body-limit=%s", config.Limit))` (middleware/body_limit.go) — this happens at middleware-construction time, before the handler is returned.
`BodyDumpWithConfig` panics with `"echo: body-dump middleware requires a handler function"` if `config.Handler` is nil (middleware/body_dump.go).
